title: Work after Imperial and the introduction to Malaco
summary: After Imperial he worked with local people, then met Walker, who connected him with Malaco Records in Mississippi, leading to Mr. Big Stuff.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: So what was, I'm moving along, after Imperial, what were your other clients after Imperial? I mean, after you?

After Imperial, I did some work with and for some people. Some people in town. Senator Jones is going to come to mind. I did some, then I met this fellow called Sigmund Walker, or whatever. I forgot his first name, Shane. But anyway, he had connection with a company in Mississippi called Malico Records. You know, they was down in the dumps here. They was doing some commercial stuff in Mississippi. That day, you know, country and western, I would imagine, type stuff. And so he went over there and he made a deal with them. And he took me over there and we introduced and came up with some work and agreement and all that kind of jazz. And that's where I had Mr. Big Stuff and-
